item.title: Inference Optimisation: Making Models Faster and Cheaper
item.description:
Simple definition#

Inference optimisation is making a model produce the same (or nearly the same) output faster, cheaper or for more users at once. It happens at three levels: the model (make it smaller or decode smarter), the hardware (use the accelerator well) and the service (schedule requests well).

item.title: Evaluating AI Systems: Criteria, Benchmarks and the Evaluation Pipeline
item.description:
Simple definition#

Evaluating an AI system means checking whether the whole application — prompts, retrieval, model, tools and guardrails — does its job well enough, safely enough and cheaply enough. It turns the methods in evaluation methodology into a repeatable pipeline that runs before every change and continuously in production.

item.title: AI Engineering Architecture: Building It Up Step by Step
item.description:
Simple definition#

Most AI applications converge on the same architecture, but no team should build it all on day one. This article grows it one component at a time, each added only when a concrete need appears: context, guardrails, routing, caching, actions — and the observability that makes all of it operable.

item.title: Designing for User Feedback and the Data Flywheel
item.description:
Simple definition#

User feedback is every signal users give — deliberately or not — about whether the application helped them. It is the one data source competitors cannot copy. Collected well, it drives evaluation (are we getting better?), development (what should we train or fix next?) and personalisation (what does this user prefer?).
